title: The Lettermen added to the Homecoming entertainment bill
why: Dropped: I read the whole index of Herald 47:7 and nothing in it, or in the 1968 Talisman, ties the Lettermen booking to student government, and the 12 October issue points to a 17 October show rather than Homecoming week.

title: Associated Students co-sponsored the musical '1776'
body: The Herald of 6 October 1970 announced that the curtain would rise the next day on the Broadway musical '1776'. Writing in the 1971 Talisman, Associated Students president John Lyne listed the co-sponsorship of '1776' among the theatrical events his government had backed as it widened its work from entertainment into cultural programmes. The same yearbook places the performance among that week's Homecoming activities.
why: Cut Jeanne Jackson's 'best ever musical', which I could not find; the checker was wrong that the 1971 Talisman has no Lyne account, so I kept the co-sponsorship and sourced it to his signed president's report at https://archive.org/details/talisman1971west.

title: Associated Students rescheduled the Isaac Hayes concert
body: The Isaac Hayes concert set for 17 February 1972 fell through when Hayes had flu, and the 1972 Talisman records that Associated Students rescheduled it for 23 March. Stephanie Madison's review in the Herald of 28 March shows the rescheduled show went ahead.
why: Kept the 23 March date after all: the checker read only the Talisman's body text, but the photograph caption in the same yearbook states the concert was rescheduled by Associated Students for March 23 (https://archive.org/details/talisman1972west).

title: Jimmy Buffett played an ASG mini-concert
body: The Herald of 17 April 1973 billed a mini-concert by Jimmy Buffett for that Thursday. The 1973 Talisman records that Buffett came to campus on 19 April in levis and a cowboy shirt carrying two Martin guitars, and counts him among the two major concerts, three mini-concerts and Bluegrass Festival that ASG sponsored that spring semester.
why: The cited Herald item is only an advance notice, so I attributed the date, the clothes, the guitars and the ASG sponsorship to the 1973 Talisman concerts section, which I read and which supplies all four (https://archive.org/details/talisman1973west).

title: ASG broke even on the Bar-Kays mini-concert
body: The Herald of 25 October 1974 billed the Bar-Kays for a mini-concert that night. The 1975 Talisman records that ASG presented the seven-member group, the backing band on Isaac Hayes's 'Hot Buttered Soul' and 'Shaft' albums, as one of its major mini-concerts of the year, and that ASG broke even on the concert.
why: Kept the money claim but moved it off the advance notice and onto the 1975 Talisman entertainment section, which I read and which states ASG broke even (https://archive.org/details/talisman1975west).

title: ASG sponsored Natalie Cole in Van Meter
body: The Herald reported on 9 December 1975 that Associated Student Government would sponsor a concert by the jazz vocalist Natalie Cole. The 1976 Talisman records that Cole, daughter of the late Nat King Cole, performed in Van Meter Auditorium on 10 December to an estimated crowd of 325, singing 'This Will Be', 'Killing Me Softly With His Song', 'Honky Tonk Women' and 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life'.
why: Left the ASG sponsorship on the cited advance notice and attributed the date, venue, crowd of 325 and songs to the 1976 Talisman, which I read and which carries all of them (https://archive.org/details/talisman1976west).

title: Jimmy Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band closed the concert year
body: The Herald announced on 25 March 1977 that a Jimmy Buffett concert was set for 27 April. The 1977 Talisman records that Buffett and the Coral Reefer Band played Diddle Arena that night, drawing three encores after a ninety-minute set from a small crowd, with highlights from 'Changes in Latitudes, Changes in Attitudes' and tunes from 'Livin' and Dyin' in 3/4 Time', 'A-1-A' and 'Havana Daydreamin''. The concert lost money, and the yearbook counts Buffett among the acts brought to Western in 1976-77 by the ASG concert programme run by activities vice president Rick Kelley.
why: Attributed the setlist and everything else about the night to the 1977 Talisman, which I read and which also supplies the ASG tie the checker could not find, through Rick Kelley's concert programme (https://archive.org/details/talisman1977west).

title: Shirley Chisholm closed the Black Awareness Symposium
body: Congresswoman Shirley Chisholm cancelled her February lecture, which is why the former Black Awareness Week was stretched across the spring semester as a symposium, and her rescheduled talk on 18 April closed it. She spoke on America's unfulfilled legacies before a crowd of about 250, predominantly black, who shouted and chanted in response, describing herself as a people's politician who could not be manipulated and saying she was there to tell people what they did not want to hear. The same yearbook records that lectures and concerts had been run by Associated Student Government until a reorganised University Center Board took them over in the autumn of 1979.

src.label: Talisman 1979, Black Awareness Symposium and lectures sections

why: Cut Van Meter, the 8 p.m. start, the word free and the claim that she filled the hall, all absent from the source, and cut the Herald's wording about cancelling all February appearances; added the sourced note on who ran lectures, since the symposium itself was coordinated by the university programs office.

title: ASG president shot in the members' assassination game
body: ASG members spent the autumn of 1986 playing an assassination game with squirt guns, sponsored by the congress's public relations committee. President Tim Todd was shot at about 8 p.m. on Thursday 2 October in his State Street apartment, wearing only a bathrobe. Kathryn Michelsen killed three other congress members the same night, including a sleeping Holger Velastegui, and three more on the Sunday, two of them in front of their girlfriends; she led the field until Gamaliel freshman Janet Dyer shot her between the eyes near the university center on the night of 8 October.

src.label: College Heights Herald 62:13, 9 Oct 1986 - Jessie, "Associated Student Government Members All Wet From Playing with Guns"

why: Reassigned the Sunday killings from Janet Dyer to Kathryn Michelsen, dated Dyer's shot to the night of 8 October, corrected toy guns to squirt guns and added the public relations committee as sponsor.

title: A bill to set up a Coach for a Game fundraiser
body: Bill 92-03-S, written by Mistianna Holcomb and sponsored by the public relations committee, proposed a Coach for a Game programme alongside the President for a Day event ASG already sponsored in the fall. It would have made it mandatory for every ASG member to sell ten raffle tickets at 50 cents each, with the proceeds going to a philanthropic cause. The document carries no introduction, reading or voting dates, so the file does not show when or whether it passed.
money: raffle tickets 50 cents each, ten per member

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-03-S, Establishment of a Coach for a Game Program

why: Cut Ralph Willard, the Central Florida game, the 29 February date, the Downing University Center ticket tables and hours, the drawing, Holcomb's job title and her quote, none of which are in the bill, and demoted the date to year only because the bill is undated.

title: $2,250 of organizational aid split between thirteen groups
body: Bill 94-2-S, introduced on 1 March 1994, disbursed the $2,250 budgeted for organizational aid after the committee spent more than four hours across three meetings deciding between the applicants. Phi Beta Sigma took $350; Alpha Phi Omega, Campus Crusade for Christ and Delta Sigma Theta took $250 each; Beta Alpha Psi $200; the Fellowship of Christian Athletes $150; the Association of Resident Assistants, the Legion of Veterans, Students' Right to Life and United Student Activists $125 each; and the International Club, SOTA and the Topperettes $100 each. It passed on second reading on 8 March 1994.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 94-2-S, Organizational Aid Recipients

why: Swapped the two amounts the checker found reversed, giving Phi Beta Sigma $350 and the Topperettes $100, and set out all thirteen grants in full so the figures add to $2,250.

title: SGA billed Dialogue Day at Java City
body: SGA's website announced on 26 October 2003 that Dialogue Day would be held the following Tuesday, 28 October, at Java City near the library from noon to 2 p.m., where students could meet WKU administrators including their deans. The surviving capture is the notice only; it does not report on the event afterwards.

src.label: WKU SGA news page, 26 Oct 2003 (Wayback capture)

why: Recast as what SGA announced rather than what happened, and cut the unsupported claim that it became a fixture repeated in later years; I read the whole capture and the later items never mention it again.

title: Campus safety walk found nearly 30 lights out
body: SGA's campus safety walk took place in the week before 10 November 2010. Reporting to the Senate, executive vice president Kendrick Bryan said participants had found nearly 30 lights that were out around campus.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 10 Nov 2010 - Stunson, "SGA invites regents to Dine with Decision Makers"

why: Cut Mike Wallace, John Osborne and the 26 October date, which came from a pre-event notice, and demoted the day because the cited article dates the walk only to the previous week.
